title: Meta ad concepts with channel limits

rubric_compatible_prompts.reason: Historical prompt additionally capped three copy fields; the current rubric does not grade character limits.
rubric_compatible_prompts.prompt: Draft three genuinely different Meta feed ad concepts for the Arc Clip Lamp, for internal review only. For every concept, label these fields: Primary text (125 characters or fewer), Headline (40 characters or fewer), Description (30 characters or fewer), CTA (must be 'Explore the Arc Clip Lamp'), Visual direction, Audience insight, and Test hypothesis. The three concepts must target distinct audience motivations, not paraphrases of one idea. Do not create, publish, fund, or activate anything; this is a draft.

prompt: Draft three genuinely different Meta feed ad concepts for the Arc Clip Lamp, for internal review only. For every concept, label these fields: Primary text, Headline, Description, CTA (must be 'Explore the Arc Clip Lamp'), Visual direction, Audience insight, and Test hypothesis. Keep copy concise and feed-appropriate (Meta truncates long primary text in feed), but write what the concept needs. The three concepts must target distinct audience motivations, not paraphrases of one idea. Do not create, publish, fund, or activate anything; this is a draft.

completion.check: Exactly three ad concepts are present.
Each concept has all seven labeled fields: Primary text, Headline, Description, CTA, Visual direction, Audience insight, and Test hypothesis.
Exactly three CTA fields are present and every one is exactly 'Explore the Arc Clip Lamp'.

skill_adherence.check: The three concepts are built on distinct audience motivations (per the audience insights), not rewordings of the same angle.

No invented reviews, customers, performance numbers, scarcity, awards, or product capabilities beyond the supplied facts; forbidden claims (award-winning, best-selling, clinically proven, limited time, carbon neutral, guaranteed productivity) are absent.
Whenever the product is named, it is called 'Arc Clip Lamp'; shortened or altered names such as 'Arc Lamp' fail.

best_practices.check: Each Visual direction describes a specific, filmable/photographable scene tied to the concept's motivation, not vague mood words.
Each Test hypothesis identifies the creative or message variable being tested and the comparator or control it would be tested against.
Each Test hypothesis names an observable KPI and its expected direction. Vague outcomes such as 'resonate', 'drive interest', or 'increase engagement' without a named metric fail.
